title: IdP compatibility guide: SAML attribute bindings, RBAC v2 mapping, and audit flow validation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Produce an IdP-specific compatibility guide and verification harness that ensures SAML assertions from Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, and Ping map cleanly into RBAC v2, and that audit logging captures SSO events at sufficient fidelity for compliance. This ticket covers attribute binding rules, precedence, group sync interplay, assertion validation edge cases, certificate rotation behavior, and recommendations for Admin Console mapping UI. Deliverables: 1) Canonical mapping table for each IdP (NameID, email, user.displayName, roles/groups, custom attributes used for RBAC), 2) Test harness and automated tests that validate mapping and audit emission, 3) Upgrade/migration notes for customers moving from RBAC v1 to v2, 4) Runbook for troubleshooting common IdP incompatibilities, 5) Confluence doc + sample SAML responses and recommended IdP settings.
acceptance_criteria: 1) For each IdP, we have a passing matrix of attribute mapping tests (okta/azure/google/ping) executed in CI. 2) RBAC v2 role bindings can be provisioned using both attribute-based roles and group-claim-based roles from each IdP. 3) Audit logs include SAML assertion fingerprint, identity.email, assertion.issue_instant, idp_entity_id, and mapping_decision with redaction rules enforced. 4) Certificate rollover scenario is exercised: automatic detection and seamless rollover without dropped sessions in canary orgs. 5) Documentation written and reviewed by Security and Product; rollout plan approved.
notes: Key trade-offs: storing raw assertions vs hashed assertion fingerprint for post-incident analysis. We choose to store a hashed fingerprint (sha256) plus the minimal unredacted attributes necessary to reconstruct event context; full raw assertions are only retained when a customer opt-in legal/compliance request is present. Assertion encryption (encrypted assertions) support is out of scope for initial rollout due to complexity and low customer demand; we will document limitations. Signature algorithm support: require RSA-SHA256; we will accept RSA-SHA1 only with explicit admin opt-in and a warning in Console. SCIM-driven groups remain preferred for large orgs; group claims are supported as fallback for customers not using SCIM.
test_cases: Okta: email attribute case-insensitive mapping and multi-valued group claim with comma separator
Azure AD: nameidentifier formats (email vs transient) and fallback to user.mail when NameID is transient
Google Workspace: groups populated via groupInSaml attribute and nested group handling simulation
Ping: support for urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent and relayState quirks
Certificate rotation: IdP publishes new signing cert; validate parallel cert acceptance window and verify rollover in 0-48h window
Clock skew: tests for up to 5m skew and test rejection beyond configured tolerance
Signature algorithm mismatch: assert rejection if not allowed unless admin override enabled
Assertion audience mismatch: reject and emit audit event with mismatch details
Replay protection: assert reuse of assertion_id is detected and logged
SCIM vs group-claim precedence: ensure SCIM-provisioned group bindings override claim-based mappings
qa_checklist: Run CI suite acquiring SAML responses from test tenants for each IdP
Manual verification for 5 sample enterprise org configurations per IdP
End-to-end test: login -> role-assigned -> API call verifying RBAC enforcement -> audit event contains mapping_decision
Canary rollout to internal orgs + 3 pilot customers with feature-flag gating
Security review sign-off and penetration checklist completed
Console UI copy updated to explain attribute precedence and opt-in flags
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flagged deploy to staging and internal Redwood orgs. 2) Canary tranche: 3 low-risk enterprise customers (consent + backup admin contact). 3) Monitor mapping_failure_rate, auth_error_rate, and audit_coverage (target >= 99%). 4) After 7 days stable, open to broader beta. 5) Full rollout with announcement and migration playbook. Emergency kill-switch: revert to existing SAML-compatible legacy mapping for orgs with critical failures.
runbook_snippets: Common fixes: - Missing email: advise Okta to include user.email as attribute statement or configure NameID-format to emailAddress. - Multi-value groups appear as single string: guide to set attribute-delimiter or use group array claims in Okta. - Azure AD transient NameID: map user.mail to preferred_username in Console mapping. - Certificate mismatch: check IdP metadata URL and validate new cert thumbprint. - Replay errors: ensure clock synchronization (ntp) and validate assertion_id uniqueness at IdP side.
